say: Ifeoma runs a lesson centre in Abuja. In March, Google Ads reported 40 leads. Her own enquiry book showed only 22.
That is 55%. Nearly half the reported leads were not real.
The cause was one setting. The form conversion counted Every, so the thank-you page fired again whenever parents refreshed it.
She spent 160,000 naira. The report said each lead cost 4,000 naira. The true figure was about 7,273 naira.
She changed Count to One. Next month Google showed 25 and her book showed 23.

Now structure. Tunde, our Ibadan solar installer, builds one Search campaign with three ad groups: solar installation, inverter installation, and repairs. Each has one clear theme, so each ad speaks to one need.

items: One theme per ad group, 3 keywords each

Negatives: jobs, vacancy, training, diy
Location option: Presence, not interest
Maximize clicks with a ₦500 CPC limit

say: Every week, open the search terms report. It shows the real searches that triggered your ads.
In Tunde's first week he spent 69,300 naira. Searches for jobs, vacancy and training cost 8,400 naira with 0 leads. That is about 12.1% of his spend, so he blocks them.

Price searches cost ₦6,300 for 1 lead. Move them to their own ad group with a pricing ad.
"inverter installation bodija" gave 3 leads for ₦2,100. Add it as an exact keyword.

say: Launch day is when most budget mistakes happen, so use this list every time.

Conversions tested. Location and language right. Budget is the monthly figure divided by 30.4, and the client has confirmed it in writing. Negatives attached. Every page opens fast on mobile. And every claim, like a price or warranty, confirmed by the client.

panel.heading: Pre-launch checklist
items: Conversions tested and counting correctly
Location set to Presence; languages right
Budget = monthly / 30.4, confirmed in writing
Negative list attached
Every page opens fast on mobile
Every claim confirmed by the client

say: Ad spend is charged to the client's own card, inside their own account. You get access through your manager account.

panel.heading: Safe money habits
left: Client pays Google from own card
right: Run client ads on your own card
Take ad spend into your account
Pay a caller claiming to be Google

say: Never run client ads on your personal card, and never take ad spend into your personal bank account. It mixes your money with theirs.
And warn clients about callers who claim to be from Google and ask for payment. Changes and billing happen inside the account, never by sending money to a person.

say: To remember. The client owns the account and pays Google directly. Make real leads your primary conversions, counted as One.
Always compare reported leads with the client's own records. Check search terms every week and add negatives. And log every change, with the reason.
